summary: Targeted retest of the currency-selector bug from iteration_3.json. Verified money() fix on Discount and Loan calculators via Playwright against http://localhost:3000. All currency-formatting checks PASS: default USD shows $, switching to EUR/INR on discount and GBP on loan updates every dynamic amount (final price, discount amount, original price, monthly payment, principal, total interest, total payment, and extra-payment savings text) with the correct symbol and no leftover '$'. Numeric values are unchanged across currencies (e.g. discount stays 60.00, loan monthly stays 386.66) confirming re-formatting rather than re-calculation. localStorage persistence verified: after selecting INR on /calculators/discount-calculator and reloading, the select value is restored to INR and all amounts render with ₹.
critical_code_review_comments: money() fix in components/calculator/impl/fields.tsx is correct — dropping the navigator.language first arg lets Intl.NumberFormat use the runtime default locale and prevents the previous throw on non-BCP-47 tags. Fallback now correctly returns `${currency} amount` instead of hardcoding '$'.

Note: static 'Worked example' tutorial text on the loan page still contains hardcoded '$20,000' / '$386.66'. Not a bug per se (it's illustrative copy), but if truly locale-agnostic content is desired later, consider parameterising it or removing the currency symbol from the tutorial.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Currency selector bug from iteration_3 is fully fixed. Discount + Loan calculators verified with USD/EUR/INR/GBP and localStorage persistence. Selects are NATIVE <select> elements (use page.select_option), not radix comboboxes. Testids: disc-currency-select, disc-input-price, disc-input-percent, loan-currency-select, loan-input-amount, loan-input-rate, loan-input-years, loan-input-extra. Result container testids: calc-result (discount) — no loan-results testid found, use body text search from 'RESULT'. Hardcoded '$' remains only in static Worked-example prose, not in reactive result panel — do not flag as regression.
rca of the issue: Original bug (iter 3): money() called new Intl.NumberFormat(navigator.language, ...) where navigator.language could be a non-BCP-47 tag causing a RangeError, and the catch fallback hardcoded '$', so every currency change silently fell back to USD symbol. Fix: use undefined for locale (runtime default) and return `${currency} amount` in catch. Confirmed working across USD/EUR/GBP/INR.
